root_cause.text: The verisilicon Hantro driver modeled i.MX8MQ G1 and G2 VPUs as separate v4l2_m2m devices, so the media scheduler allowed both hardware blocks to decode concurrently despite a platform limitation that they cannot run at the same time.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that on i.MX8MQ “the g1 VPU and g2 VPU cannot decode simultaneously” and that the fix is to make “g1 and g2 share the same v4l2_m2m_dev” so scheduling enforces alternating operation; the patch adds `shared_devices`, introduces `hantro_get_v4l2_m2m_dev()`, and replaces per-device `v4l2_m2m_init()` with shared `m2m_dev` acquisition.

intent_record.intent_summary: Document the shared_devices field in struct hantro_variant to clarify that it lists device IDs that must not run concurrently.
intent_record.what: A new documentation comment line was added to the struct hantro_variant kernel-doc block, documenting a @shared_devices field as "an array of device ids that cannot run concurrently".
intent_record.how: This change does not alter runtime behavior; it only updates the struct documentation to describe the purpose of a shared_devices field, improving code clarity for developers.

intent_record.intent_summary: Extend hantro_variant with a shared_devices OF match table pointer to support tracking shared device associations for each variant.
intent_record.what: A new field named shared_devices of type const struct of_device_id * was added to struct hantro_variant after the existing bitfield members.
intent_record.how: This extends the hantro_variant structure so each variant can optionally hold a pointer to a table of OF device identifiers for shared devices, enabling later code to associate and look up such device-matching data at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add the OF platform header so the source can use or compile against device-tree platform helper APIs.
intent_record.what: A single header include was added to the file: `#include <linux/of_platform.h>` inserted alongside the existing Linux device tree and platform-related includes.
intent_record.how: This makes declarations from `linux/of_platform.h` available during compilation, enabling use of OF platform helper APIs in this source file and preventing build issues if such symbols are referenced.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add helper logic to reuse a shared v4l2 mem2mem device from related VPU instances, falling back to creating a new one when none is available.
intent_record.what: A new helper function, hantro_get_v4l2_m2m_dev(), was added. It checks whether the device variant defines shared_devices, iterates over matching device tree nodes, looks up each corresponding platform device, gets its driver data as a hantro_dev, skips invalid or self references, increments the reference count of an existing shared_vpu->m2m_dev with v4l2_m2m_get(), and returns that shared m2m device after releasing the platform device and node references. If no usable shared device is found, it falls back to creating a new m2m device with v4l2_m2m_init(&vpu_m2m_ops).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this enables a Hantro device to reuse an already initialized v4l2_m2m_dev from another related device described in shared_devices instead of always creating its own instance. This supports shared mem2mem infrastructure across multiple VPU devices, while safely ignoring missing, invalid, or self-matching devices and preserving object lifetime through reference counting.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use a Hantro-specific helper to obtain the V4L2 mem2mem device during probe instead of calling the generic initializer directly.
intent_record.what: In hantro_probe(), the assignment of vpu->m2m_dev was changed from a direct call to v4l2_m2m_init(&vpu_m2m_ops) to a call to hantro_get_v4l2_m2m_dev(vpu), while the surrounding error handling using IS_ERR() and PTR_ERR() remains unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, mem2mem device initialization is no longer performed unconditionally through the generic initializer and is instead delegated to a Hantro-specific helper that can choose how to obtain or initialize the v4l2 mem2mem device based on the vpu context, enabling driver-specific handling without changing the existing probe error path.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use v4l2_m2m_put() in hantro_probe() error cleanup to correctly drop the mem2mem device reference during probe failure.
intent_record.what: In the error path of hantro_probe(), the call to v4l2_m2m_release(vpu->m2m_dev) after media_device_cleanup(&vpu->mdev) was replaced with v4l2_m2m_put(vpu->m2m_dev).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the probe failure cleanup now decrements the mem2mem device reference using the matching put-style API instead of directly releasing it, which aligns teardown with reference-counted lifetime management and avoids incorrect cleanup behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use v4l2_m2m_put() in the remove path to correctly release the mem2mem device through reference-counted cleanup.
intent_record.what: In hantro_remove(), the call to v4l2_m2m_release(vpu->m2m_dev) was replaced with v4l2_m2m_put(vpu->m2m_dev).
intent_record.how: At runtime, the remove path now decrements the mem2mem device reference using the put-style API instead of directly releasing it, aligning teardown with reference-counted lifetime management and preventing incorrect cleanup behavior.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add an init-time device-tree match table for i.MX8MQ VPU G1/G2 shared resource handling.
intent_record.what: A new static const __initconst array of struct of_device_id named imx8mq_vpu_shared_resources was added, containing two compatible entries for "nxp,imx8mq-vpu-g1" and "nxp,imx8mq-vpu-g2", followed by a sentinel terminator.
intent_record.how: This introduces a device-tree match table that can be used during initialization to identify the i.MX8MQ VPU G1 and G2 devices as a shared resource group, enabling later init-time code to look them up or coordinate shared resource handling for those compatibles.

intent_record.intent_summary: Assign the shared resource list to the imx8mq VPU G1 variant so it correctly uses shared devices at runtime.
intent_record.what: A new struct field initializer was added to the imx8mq_vpu_g1_variant hantro_variant definition, setting .shared_devices = imx8mq_vpu_shared_resources.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the imx8mq_vpu_g1_variant now advertises and uses the shared resource/device list associated with imx8mq_vpu_shared_resources, enabling shared resource handling for this variant that was previously unspecified.

intent_record.intent_summary: Configure the imx8mq VPU G2 variant to use the shared resource list so shared-device handling works correctly for this hardware.
intent_record.what: A new struct field initializer was added to the imx8mq_vpu_g2_variant definition, setting .shared_devices = imx8mq_vpu_shared_resources.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the imx8mq VPU G2 variant will now be associated with the shared resource/device list referenced by imx8mq_vpu_shared_resources, enabling it to participate in shared-device handling that was previously not configured for this variant.

consistency_review.core_intent: Add support for sharing VPU-related resources across related Hantro variants by introducing variant-level shared-device match metadata and logic to discover and reuse shared instances on i.MX8MQ.
Switch mem2mem device cleanup to use v4l2_m2m_put() so references are released correctly in both probe-error and remove paths.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly documents the concurrency restriction mechanism (`shared_devices`) that exists to prevent certain VPUs from running at the same time, which is the core issue behind modeling i.MX8MQ G1/G2 as independently schedulable devices.

The changes explicitly add shared-device metadata and reuse logic for i.MX8MQ G1/G2 so related Hantro instances can share a single v4l2_m2m device/resource context, directly addressing the root cause that modeling them as separate m2m devices allowed forbidden concurrent decoding.

Adding an OF platform header is a build/API include change for device-tree helpers and does not address the driver modeling or scheduling issue that allowed i.MX8MQ G1 and G2 VPUs to run concurrently.

The change only switches probe-time mem2mem device initialization to a Hantro-specific helper. By itself, that does not address the root cause of modeling i.MX8MQ G1 and G2 as separate schedulable v4l2_m2m devices or preventing concurrent decoding between them.

These changes only fix reference-counted cleanup of the v4l2_m2m device in probe/remove paths. They do not address the root cause of modeling i.MX8MQ G1 and G2 as separate mem2mem devices or preventing concurrent decoding by the two hardware blocks.

The root cause is incorrect modeling of i.MX8MQ G1/G2 as independent devices despite shared hardware constraints. Assigning the shared resource list to the imx8mq G1 variant directly addresses that shared-device/runtime coordination issue.

The change makes the i.MX8MQ G2 variant use shared resources/shared-device handling, directly addressing the root cause that G1 and G2 were modeled independently and could be scheduled concurrently despite needing mutual exclusion.

candidates.rationale: This closes the imx8mq_vpu_g1_variant definition without any shared-device metadata, causing the G1 instance to be modeled independently and allowing concurrent scheduling with G2 on hardware that cannot run both at once.
This closes the imx8mq_vpu_g2_variant definition without any shared-device metadata, so G2 is also treated as an independent mem2mem device, enabling unsafe concurrent decode with G1.

vuln_statements.explanation: This closing statement terminates the imx8mq_vpu_g1_variant definition without any shared-device metadata, leaving the G1 block modeled as an independent v4l2_m2m device and allowing concurrent scheduling with G2 despite the platform restriction.

This closing statement terminates the imx8mq_vpu_g2_variant definition without any shared-device metadata, leaving the G2 block modeled as an independent v4l2_m2m device and allowing concurrent scheduling with G1 despite the platform restriction.
